body: Sunday, August 02 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The Warsh-led Fed held rates steady at its July 29 meeting but delivered a hawkish hold — three officials dissented in favor of a hike. Fiscal policy remains expansionary under Trump. The 10Y yield is surging at 4.74% (+25 bps vs 4W ago) while the 2Y has risen less, to 4.28% (prior close, +14 bps vs 4W), steepening the curve to +47bps — positively sloped but still flat by historical standards, and one that now reflects term-premium repricing rather than easing expectations. Oil ripping +23.3% in four weeks is an unambiguous stagflationary input.

New / Most Important: The three-dissent hawkish hold is structurally significant. This is the first time under Warsh's chairmanship that the committee has been this visibly split. Warsh stated the Fed "won't hesitate to stop inflation," but the bond market has doubts — hence yields climbing on term premium rather than short-rate expectations. The headline that "GDP growth is stronger than it looks" combined with the Washington Post flagging that "the biggest gamble in the U.S. economy is starting to look riskier" paints a picture of above-trend nominal growth masking deteriorating real fundamentals. Meanwhile, Amazon nearly doubling its debt to $129B in six months to fund $220B in data center capex is the single most important corporate capital-flow signal of the week — this is fiscal-scale private-sector spending being financed in a rising-rate environment. Friday's jobs report looms as the week's key catalyst.

Playbook ✓: S&P 500 at 7489 (↑0.1%) is flatlined at highs — mega-cap resilience masking breadth stress is textbook late-cycle. VIX at 16.0 screams complacency.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The Nasdaq 100 is DOWN 3.6% over four weeks while the Russell 2000 is only down 2.2% — small-caps are actually outperforming large-cap tech in a rising-rate, rising-oil environment. This is not the playbook. Rising long-end yields should punish duration-sensitive small-caps more, yet the Russell/Nasdaq ratio is ↑1.5%. This suggests the Nasdaq selloff is AI-specific (valuation compression on capex concerns) rather than macro-driven. The rotation is telling us that the market is starting to price "real economy over AI narrative" — a theme that has legs if oil stays elevated and the Fed stays hawkish. Watch this ratio closely as it may signal a regime shift in equity leadership.

Macro Stance: The ECB is now on course to raise rates again in September after eurozone inflation surprised to the upside at 2.9% in July. Higher energy prices are the proximate cause. Despite the ECB wage tracker detecting no pickup in wage pressures, headline inflation re-accelerating is forcing the Governing Council's hand.

New / Most Important: This is a structurally important moment for the eurozone. The ECB is being forced into a hiking posture at a time when the underlying economy is fragile and the inflation impulse is largely exogenous (energy, not wages). This is a classic policy trap: tightening into a cost-push shock that monetary policy cannot resolve. The euro is rising on rate-hike bets, which will tighten financial conditions further via the exchange rate channel. For capital flows, a hawkish ECB plus a hawkish-hold Fed compresses the transatlantic rate differential — this could pull capital toward European fixed income at the margin, but the equity implication is unambiguously negative for cyclicals. The absence of wage pressures is the ECB's own data telling it not to hike, yet headline CPI politics will override. This sets up a potential policy error that could show up in peripheral spreads by Q4.

Playbook ✓: Euro strengthening on rate expectations is textbook.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Hiking into an energy cost shock without wage confirmation is fighting the wrong war. If oil stays elevated (↑23.3% in 4 weeks per quant snapshot), the ECB will be tightening into the precise headwind it cannot control.

Macro Stance: Policy rates are on hold, the easing bias is explicit, and the currency has become the constraint. The PBOC set the overnight reverse repo rate steady at 1.25% (Reuters, [Jul 28]) and maintained liquidity support before month-end (TradingView, [Jul 28]); one read of the Politburo is that RRR and rate cuts are likely in Q3 (BigGo Finance, [Jul 30]). The yuan hit a three-year high despite the PBOC signalling discomfort over the gains (The Edge Malaysia, [Jul 31]), and the central bank is leaning against the rally with a stable daily fix (The Business Times, [Jul 31]). June CPI rose only 1% (Global Times, [Jul 9]) while PPI climbed 4.1% (finance.biggo.com, [Jul 8]), a margin squeeze rather than demand-pull reflation.

PMIs & Activity: The official manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.2 (The State Council Information Office, [Jul 31]) and the non-manufacturing PMI to 49 (Macau Business, [Jul 31]), as factories and construction slumped together (The Edge Malaysia, [Jul 31]) and services returned to contraction (TradingView, [Jul 31]). Against June's 50.3 (Reuters, [Jun 29]) this is a clean break, which CNBC ties to a demand slump and typhoons ([Jul 30]). Exports are no longer a reliable offset, with US-bound shipments falling in July after a brief recovery (CNBC, [Jul 30]). Q2 GDP grew 4.3%, below the target range (Bloomberg, [Jul 15]), and first-half industrial profits rose 18.7% as a tech boom masks the property slump (Caixin Global, [Jul 27]). The consumer is the weak leg: Nike's China sales have fallen 30% (CNBC, [Jul 29]) and the China slump hit BMW's earnings (RTE.ie, [Jul 30]).

Credit Impulse: June new bank loans rose less than expected (The Star, [Jul 15]) and credit growth missed forecasts as the PBOC flagged a "new normal" (Caixin Global, [Jul 16]); household loans fell by 366.8 billion yuan in the first half (36Kr, [Jul 17]). Cash at Chinese banks has swelled to a record as borrowing slows (Nikkei Asia, [Jul 28]): liquidity is ample, credit demand is not. The biggest banks have launched their first repo-linked loans (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 27]), but a dip in the debt ratio may not bode well for the economy (South China Morning Post, [Jul 31]), even as the local government debt clean-up makes progress (ISI Markets, [Aug 1]). The impulse reads flat, with households negative.

Property: June new home prices fell at a slower pace (Reuters, [Jul 14]) and first-tier prices extended a four-month rebound (South China Morning Post, [Jul 15]), but resale prices fell faster (Reuters, [Jun 30]) and property investment slumped 18 percent y/y in January–June (The Standard (HK), [Jul 15]). The demand base is eroding: Chinese families are walking away from homes and into portfolios (South China Morning Post, [Aug 1]), and July was China's worst building month since Covid (Wood Central, [Aug 1]). Vanke completed a board reshuffle as Xu Enli takes the helm for a turnaround battle (finance.biggo.com, [Jul 31]), and in Hong Kong builder Parkview missed an interest payment on a loan (The Business Times, [Jul 30]).

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: The Politburo read has settled on incremental policy support (Caixin Global, [Jul 31]), a fiscal push without big stimulus (VT Markets, [Jul 31]). Leaders pledged to support the economy without big new stimulus plans (Reuters, [Jul 30]), while Bloomberg reports top officials will consider new stimulus after the slowdown ([Jul 30]). Reconciled: incremental measures now, a larger package only if the data worsen, and July's PMIs are the first test. On trade, the US urged China to "fully meet" its rare-earths pledge (Nikkei Asia, [Jul 31]), China voiced "serious concern" over new US curbs (South China Morning Post, [Jul 31]) and a Trump-Xi September summit is taking shape (Firstpost, [Jul 31]); China says the US pledged to cap replacement tariffs at 20% (Bloomberg, [Jul 27]).

Markets & Flows: Chinese stocks are on track for their worst month in a decade (Financial Times, [Jul 30]) as chip stocks slump on a rotation away from tech (Bloomberg, [Jul 30]); AI IPOs have failed to lift the market (International Business Times, [Jul 31]), though the Politburo bolstered hope the state will support stocks (South China Morning Post, [Jul 31]). The PBOC is set to further boost panda bond issuance (China Daily, [Jul 31]), China completed its first Malaysia payment in digital yuan (South China Morning Post, [Aug 1]), and central banks led by China drove record Q2 gold demand (TipRanks, [Jul 30]).

New / Most Important: The construction leg is now the story. The non-manufacturing PMI at 49 captures what Wood Central calls the worst building month since Covid, and SCMP describes households shifting savings from homes to portfolios: property is losing its buyers, not only its builders. Leaders committed only to incremental support, so the lever is monetary, with RRR and rate cuts the base case, but a yuan at a three-year high tightens conditions for exporters as US-bound shipments roll over. BYD's overseas push on flash-charging technology shows where growth still is: abroad.

Playbook ✓: Incremental Politburo support, liquidity easing, weak property and a managed trade truce heading into a September summit are on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The consensus treated the Politburo as the turning point; instead July's PMIs show contraction broadening to construction and services, with property investment down 18 percent. Iron ore eased as faltering China demand offset stimulus hopes (Business Recorder, [Jul 28]) and NZD/USD slipped to 0.5860 on weak China PMIs (VT Markets, [Jul 31]); the Australian dollar inched lower as China's NBS manufacturing PMI fell (www.tmgm.com, [Jul 31]). European carmakers absorb a deepening China slump, EM equity flows suffer as Chinese stocks head for their worst month in a decade, and oil at $84.67 stays a terms-of-trade tax on China's margins.

Macro Stance: The BOJ held rates at 1% on July 31 but explicitly warned that core inflation is exceeding its 2% target and signaled commitment to further hikes. Suspected yen intervention occurred ahead of the meeting, confirming the currency remains a policy priority. The BOJ is now the most hawkishly-signaling it has been in decades.

New / Most Important: The BOJ's simultaneous rate hold + hawkish forward guidance + yen intervention is a three-pronged signal that September is live for a hike. This is structurally important for global capital flows: a BOJ hike would narrow the USD-JPY carry trade spread further, potentially triggering another wave of carry unwind. Last year's carry unwind in August 2024 caused significant global market dislocations. The fact that the BOJ is telegraphing this so clearly suggests they want to avoid a disorderly market reaction, but the carry trade community is larger and more leveraged than official communication can fully manage. Any September hike combined with a weakening dollar would create a JPY rally that forces cross-asset deleveraging. The MUFG note flagging "suspected JPY intervention" confirms authorities are already actively managing the transition.

Playbook ✓: Gradual normalization path is consensus.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The speed of signaling — moving from "chance of early hike" to "committed to more hikes" in a single meeting — is faster than markets expected. Watch JGB yields and JPY crosses for stress signals.

Macro Stance: Inflation eased to 3.8%, undershooting forecasts and significantly reducing the probability of further rate hikes. Markets have pared rate-hike bets sharply. RBA Governor Bullock left the threat of higher rates on the table rhetorically but acknowledged housing has eased "more than anticipated."

New / Most Important: The inflation undershoot is the cleanest positive macro surprise globally this week. Traders have axed hike bets — this is a meaningful shift in the rates market.  |  Playbook ✓: AUD and rate-sensitive equities should benefit from reduced tightening risk.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Bullock's refusal to fully close the door on hikes while inflation is clearly decelerating suggests the RBA is still fighting the last war. If oil's surge (↑23.3%) feeds through to Australian petrol prices, the RBA may get whipsawed back into hawkishness — creating a communication credibility problem.

Macro Stance: The weekend reading of Friday's GUS flash is settling into consensus: July CPI rose to 3.0% y/y (Miesięcznik Finansowy BANK, [Jul 31]) with fuel up around 14% in a month (Obserwator Gospodarczy, [Jul 31]) after the government's fuel shield expired (Magazyn MANAGER+, [Aug 1]), while food prices fell and are what keeps the index in check (xyz.pl, [Aug 2]). The policy read is uniform: Global Banking & Finance Review [Jul 31] says the print strengthens the rate-hold outlook, both the Rzeczpospolita and Parkiet economist panels [Jul 31] say the RPP should not rush to cut and Citi's above-3.5% year-end call stands as the direct read-through from the global oil spike. Growth makes patience cheap: GUS statistics show Poland growing twice as fast as the EU as a whole (Agro Profil, [Jul 31]). Politically the fuel shock is biting: 54% of Poles rate the government's handling of fuel prices badly in a new DGP poll (Gazeta Prawna, [Aug 2]). Stance: hold, with the earlier market hopes for H2 cuts now looking stale.

Markets: The week closed on a record. Business Insider Polska [Jul 31] wrote that July 31 went into the history of the Polish exchange; FXMAG [Jul 31] had WIG20 a step from the 4000-point barrier with KGHM and banks pulling it up, and Bankier [Jul 31] summed up a superb month with WIG20 one step from the record and Żabka taken over. Friday's leadership rotated away from banks: Żabka led the gains with energy names strongly higher (Inwestycje.pl, [Jul 31]), which the card confirms with PGE back above 10 at 10.11 (-3.5% 1W, +5.0% 4W) and Orlen 148.04 (-5.1% 1W, +11.4% 4W) steadying after Comparic [Jul 31] asked whether its post-rally slide is a correction or something bigger. Banks gave a little back but keep the weekly lead: PKO 111.92 (+5.0% 1W, +6.3% 4W), Pekao 245.5 (+5.0% 1W, +5.3% 4W). Consumer and growth names led the month: Dino 31.99 (+11.2% 1W, +15.5% 4W), LPP 21,720 (+7.8% 1W, +17.1% 4W), CD Projekt 249.9 (+10.5% 1W, +7.1% 4W), Allegro 44.99 (+17.0% 4W); KGHM 307.95 is +1.5% 1W but still -8.1% 4W. EPOL 42.83 is +4.7% 1W and +8.6% 4W. The zloty is firm: USD/PLN 3.7357 (-1.8% 1W, -0.4% 4W) with the dollar back near 3.75 after the Fed (Magazyn MANAGER+, [Jul 31]), EUR/PLN 4.3051 (-0.6% 1W, +0.4% 4W), and ING argues the zloty has room to rally once the dollar squeeze passes (Exchange Rates UK, [Aug 1]). Bonds: yields had risen worryingly ahead of the Fed (Subiektywnie o finansach, [Jul 29]).

Fiscal & Politics: The Sejm granted the government discharge for the 2025 budget amid a bitter row over the deficit (Strefa Biznesu, [Jul 31]), and the debt argument has turned into a blame game: President Nawrocki is pushing a deficit "hammer" with penalties for politicians who overspend (BitHub.pl, [Aug 1]), while government communicators try to pin the state of public finances on the president (wPolityce.pl, [Aug 1]). The numbers behind the fight: debt above 2 trillion zł (naTemat.pl, [Jul 27]), Arak's forecast of more than 70% of GDP by end-2027 (Filary Biznesu, [Jul 26]) and wnp.pl's [Jul 26] warning of EU sanctions. Fuel policy is stuck: Domański says the CPN package has no financing after the president's decision (Money.pl, [Jul 31]), even as Bloomberg [Jul 27] reported the government considering revived fuel-price caps. The higher tax-free allowance may be spread over three years (Business Insider Polska, [Jul 31]) and Domański revealed Trump raised tariffs on Poland over the digital tax (Do Rzeczy, [Jul 31]).

Corporate & Sectors: Couche-Tard's roughly $8.7 billion purchase of Żabka, Poland's biggest-ever deal (Reuters, [Jul 31]), dominates; Subiektywnie o finansach [Jul 31] weighs the consequences of a Circle K owner controlling the chain. Banks: Pekao's results show a machine at full speed but a new risk (Subiektywnie o finansach, [Jul 31]), four banks nudged rates up despite the RPP hold (Bankier, [Jul 31]) and a CJEU and Supreme Court turn in CHF cases gives banks a chance to gain (Interia Biznes, [Jul 31]). Consumer-credit litigation is the counterweight: Millennium has stopped charging interest on loan costs and clients may recover overpayments (Franknews.pl, [Aug 2]); borrowers get 60 days to choose a new rate formula (wnp.pl, [Jul 31]). Housing: the government offers new home loans at a 400 zł instalment over 15 years (Portal Samorządowy, [Aug 2]) alongside BGK guarantees (Bankier, [Jul 30]). Retail: Dino and its unions set new mediation dates (Farmer.pl, [Aug 1]) after the labour ministry intervened (Business Insider Polska, [Jul 30]); Allegro was ordered to change how it shows delivery options (Telepolis.pl, [Aug 1]). Energy: gas-fired generation is up 19% (GlobEnergia, [Aug 1]), the government adopted the NECP update with new duties for energy-intensive firms from 2027 (INFOR.PL, [Aug 1]), and Hungary is shutting the Paks nuclear plant as the Danube dries (XYZ, [Aug 2]), a regional supply shock.

Geopolitics & Security: The missile aftermath continues: the military explained why the Russian Kh-101 was not shot down (WNP.PL, [Aug 1]), the foreign ministry answered Moscow (Fakt, [Aug 1]), and EUobserver [Aug 1] framed the six-minute scare as proof NATO spots threats fast but decides slowly. Deputy defence minister Tomczyk said nobody will build a Patriot factory where bombs fall as Trump refuses Ukraine (Wyborcza.pl, [Aug 2]); 100 kilometres of the eastern fortification line are ready (RMF24, [Jul 31]).

New / Most Important: The fiscal blame game. With CPI back at 3% on fuel, the one thing that could blunt it, a financed CPN package, died on the president's desk, and the two branches are now arguing over who ruined the public finances rather than how to fund anything. For bondholders a president demanding a deficit hammer is marginally supportive; for equities it means no fiscal cushion if oil runs again, and the record-high index is leaning entirely on earnings and the Żabka bid.

Playbook ✓: Hold posture consistent with sticky inflation; the record close with rotation into energy and consumer names is healthy breadth, not a top.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The oil pass-through risk makes any near-term easing impossible despite earlier market hopes for H2 cuts — and with no financed fuel shield, the next leg of pump prices goes straight into CPI.

Macro Stance: South Korea's stock market plunged as the AI-driven boom faded, with 7 in 10 stocks falling in July — the steepest monthly decline since 2008. The correction exposed Korea's dangerous economic dependency on semiconductors. This is a structural vulnerability: when a single sector represents both the equity market's marginal buyer narrative AND the economy's export engine, any global rotation away from AI capex hits Korea like a levered bet unwinding. Top investors bought Samsung on the dip, but the macro message is clear — Korea needs the AI capex cycle to persist, and signals from Amazon's debt-fueled spending and the Guardian's "opaque AI economy" headline suggest the market is beginning to question returns on that capex.
🇵🇰 Pakistan: SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% — still constrained by inflation and geopolitical risks. No room for easing.

Narrative: The Nasdaq 100 is down 3.6% over four weeks, the worst major index, as the AI capex story comes under siege — Amazon nearly doubling its debt to $129B for data centres — and a 10Y at 4.74% (+25 bps vs 4W) compresses multiples.

Reported: Apple dropped the most in 16 months on a disappointing outlook (AFR, [Aug 1]) after a forecast dogged by supply-chain struggles (Reuters, [Jul 30]). Microsoft beat with $90B in revenue and its shares jumped 9% (KOMO, [Jul 29]), saying cash will keep flowing from AI (Reuters, [Jul 31]). Fair Isaac plunged 17% on mixed results and a delay in a key program (TIKR.com, [Jul 31]).

EPS Upside Watch: Palantir — reports this week (TradingKey, [Aug 1]), with one pro seeing a big earnings beat and $200 as realistic (24/7 Wall St., [Jul 27]). Unity Software — earnings are expected to grow (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 30]), and the shares may move 11% on the August release (Investing.com, [Jul 30]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Cathie Wood selling $5.5M of a surging tech stock is a counter-signal from a manager usually last to sell momentum; with the Nasdaq lagging the Russell, even committed growth bulls are rotating.

Narrative: Alphabet's $29B Berkshire position signals Buffett sees value in the ad and cloud duopoly, but Google's off-balance-sheet AI chip financing is a risk factor the market has not fully priced.

Reported: Meta sank 9% after its Q3 revenue forecast missed estimates (Investing.com, [Jul 29]), with profit hit by higher costs (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jul 29]). Reddit sank 11% on 'choppy' search referrals even as its results blew past estimates (CNBC, [Jul 30]). Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft added nearly $1.5 trillion in combined value in the week (CNBC, [Jul 31]).

EPS Upside Watch: Verizon — analysts raised their forecasts after its better-than-expected Q2 (Benzinga, [Jul 27]). Sony — raised guidance as its Q1 profit beat on a strong gaming business (Reuters, [Jul 30]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Google's synthetic financing of AI chip procurement echoes pre-GFC structured finance: if hyperscalers use it widely, aggregate AI capex is larger than balance sheets show. The market paid Alphabet anyway while selling Meta's cost line, so disclosure, not spending, is the risk it has not priced.

Narrative: A steepening curve (+47bps 10s-2s, 12 bps wider over four weeks) supports bank NIMs, though it is still flat by historical standards, and rising yields without a recession are the financials sweet spot.

Reported: Visa beat on cross-border volume strength (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 29]) and announced layoffs, margin expansion on top of volume. Deutsche Bank's profit rose 10%, defying an expected decline, as its investment bank boomed (Reuters, [Jul 29]). Barclays' profit rose 17% on an equities boom, but its shares fell as costs are set to rise (Reuters, [Jul 28]).

EPS Upside Watch: PayPal — raised full-year EPS guidance (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 28]), and analysts boosted their forecasts after the upbeat Q2 (Benzinga, [Jul 29]). NatWest — raised guidance and brought forward its buyback plans (WSJ, [Jul 31]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Friendly fraud is surging — 158 million chargeback disputes in 2025, up 29% — a hidden tax on e-commerce that favours incumbent processors with dispute-resolution tools: long Visa and Mastercard, short disruptors such as BNPL and neobanks that lack fraud infrastructure.

Narrative: WTI at $84.67 (↑23.3% in four weeks) is the dominant signal, Exxon's CEO Woods says "I wouldn't hold my breath" on lower gas prices, and with China's July PMIs in contraction (manufacturing 49.2, non-manufacturing 49) this is a supply shock, not a demand-led rally.

Reported: Chevron posted its highest quarterly profit in six years and beat estimates (Reuters, [Jul 31]) as refining margins soared, while rival Exxon missed (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 31]) despite profit at a four-year high (Reuters, [Jul 31]). Shell's profit more than doubled to $9.8 billion, its second-highest on record, as the Iran war lifted prices (Reuters, [Jul 30]).

EPS Upside Watch: Targa Resources — expected to beat earnings estimates into its Q2 release (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 30]). SLB — raised its outlook as data-centre revenue leapt 80%, and analysts lifted price targets (BigGo Finance, [Jul 27]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The playbook says rising oil makes the Fed tighten and demand destruction follows, but a persistent geopolitical supply shock takes quarters to destroy demand. With every major central bank tightening into a shock it cannot control, energy is the best hedge against a synchronized policy error.

Narrative: Data-centre construction — Amazon's $220B capex program — creates heavy demand for electrical equipment, HVAC and construction services, GE Aerospace near buy points is the bellwether, and small-cap outperformance (Russell/Nasdaq ratio ↑1.5%) helps domestic industrials.

Reported: Schneider Electric lifted its 2026 outlook as data-centre demand surged (Reuters, [Jul 30]). Quanta Services jumped 17% after topping consensus estimates and raising guidance (TIKR.com, [Jul 31]). GE Aerospace rose in its buy zone after an earnings letdown (Investor's Business Daily, [Jul 31]).
EPS Upside Watch: Proto Labs — lifted guidance on new data-centre and defence clients (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 31]). Axon — expected to beat earnings estimates (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 29]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The AI boom is lifting industrial stocks (Axios, [Jul 31]) to valuations as rich as tech (CNBC, [Jul 26]): the old-economy sector now carries tech-style multiple risk, while UPS dropping on a Q3 revenue warning after a beat and raised outlook (Tech Times, [Jul 28]) shows the non-AI half gets no such credit.

Narrative: Oil up 23% in four weeks is a direct tax on the consumer, US stocks sit at record highs while everyday Americans are struggling, and retirees spending nearly $1 of every $3 on a single expense constrain discretionary power.

Reported: Amazon soared 12% (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 31]) after lifting investment plans on strong cloud sales (Reuters, [Jul 31]), though it hiked 2026 capex to $220 billion on higher memory costs (CNBC, [Jul 30]). Ford jumped 4% on a Q2 beat and a guidance upgrade (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 28]) as wealthy buyers kept truck demand humming (Reuters, [Jul 28]). Crocs beat sales expectations, but the stock dropped 12.7% (StockStory, [Jul 30]).
EPS Upside Watch: Cracker Barrel — earnings estimates are rising (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 31]). Starbucks — CNBC is raising its price target after a home-run quarter (CNBC, [Jul 29]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Ford beating on wealthy buyers' trucks while everyday Americans struggle is the K-shaped consumer inside one sector: the top end carries discretionary earnings, so beats can coexist with a bearish lower-income backdrop until the oil shock reaches the top end too.
Narrative: Defensive rotation should help staples in a rising-rate, rising-oil, falling-Nasdaq market, but energy-driven input-cost inflation eats margins.

Reported: Coca-Cola beat Q2 forecasts and its shares jumped 6% (Investing.com, [Jul 28]) as it raised guidance on a World Cup sales lift (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 28]). Procter & Gamble beat estimates but the stock fell (Barron's, [Jul 29]) as it forecast slower annual sales growth with costs weighing (Reuters, [Jul 29]). Colgate beat on strong margins as sales rose 4.9% (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 31]).
EPS Upside Watch: Tyson Foods — analysts predict a rise in its third-quarter earnings (Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette, [Jul 31]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The haven is priced like growth: Coca-Cola hit an all-time high with a P/E now topping some AI leaders (BigGo Finance, [Jul 28]) while Q3 estimates are falling for consumer staples (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 29]). The defensive bid is running ahead of the earnings, so cost-hit prints like P&G's get sold.
Narrative: Eli Lilly's earnings loom this week, while RFK Jr. trending on X keeps pharma in a regulatory fog — a classic uncertainty-discount sector.

Reported: Bristol Myers Squibb raised its 2026 forecast after a Q2 beat (Quartz, [Jul 30]). AbbVie topped Q2 estimates but trimmed its 2026 profit view on the Apogee deal (Reuters, [Jul 31]), and its shares were pressured as the beat fell below investor expectations (BioSpace, [Jul 31]). Alnylam tanked 28% on a Q2 miss and a cut to its 2026 sales view (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 31]).

EPS Upside Watch: Biogen — flipped its 2026 guidance from an expected decline to a sales increase (Fierce Pharma, [Jul 29]) as new medicines overtake its MS business (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 29]). Labcorp — raised its earnings outlook on strong medical testing demand (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 30]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: RFK Jr.'s HHS leadership is a policy overhang with no precedent for pharma, and elevated public engagement with health policy can turn into legislation. As long as Kennedy holds the post, the sector's discount may be structural rather than cyclical, whatever the beats.

Narrative: Copper at 6.47 (↑5.7%) is supportive as an AI data-centre and grid-capex metal. China's demand signal is weak — iron ore eased and July was China's worst building month since Covid — so the edge sits with copper miners as an AI and grid-capex play.

Reported: Rio Tinto posted a 43% jump in first-half earnings as the data-centre boom boosted copper (Reuters, [Jul 29]). Linde beat Q2 forecasts on strong electronics demand and lifted its outlook (Reuters, [Jul 31]). Corteva raised its full-year profit forecast, but its shares fell after a revenue miss (Reuters, [Jul 30]).

EPS Upside Watch: Worthington Steel — earnings estimates are moving higher (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 29]). International Paper — Truist raised its price target on the earnings beat (Investing.com, [Jul 31]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Rio Tinto is buoyant on AI demand for metals (Financial Times, [Jul 29]), but re-rating miners on data-centre copper ties them to the AI capex cycle, so the Korea-led AI hardware wobble becomes a materials risk too.
